task: Compare how the corpus describes DVC versus model registries. What problem does each solve?
final_answer: DVC versions *data*: it solves the problem that Git is a poor fit for large files by storing content hashes in Git while keeping the actual data in a remote backend (S3, GCS, etc.), so any Git commit corresponds to an exact snapshot of both code and data [doc6_data_versioning.md]. A model registry versions *models*: it solves the lifecycle-management problem by storing model artifacts with metadata (training data version, metrics, hyperparameters) and lifecycle stages (Staging, Production, Archived), serving as the single source of truth between training and deployment [doc7_model_registry.md]. Together they close the reproducibility loop — the registry records which data version trained each model.
